chunks: There is no harm in his performing the prayer of the night and the day with one tayammum, so long as he does not break his state of purity or find water.
As for the report which he narrated:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Abi Hammam, from al-Rida عليه السلام.
He said: 'One performs tayammum for every salat (prayer) until water is found.'
And this hadith was narrated by:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Abbas, from Abi Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام.
He said: 'Nothing is enjoyed by means of tayammum except one salat (prayer) and its supererogatory prayer.'

These two hadiths differ in wording while the narrator is one, because Abi Hammam narrated from al-Rida عليه السلام in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, while in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, yet the ruling is one. This is among what weakens using the report as proof. Then even if the report were sound, it would be understood as recommendation, just as renewing wudu (ablution) is understood as recommendation, although there is no disagreement concerning the permissibility of many prayers by means of it. It is also possible that what was meant was that one performs tayammum for every salat (prayer) if he had become able to access water between the two prayers, because once it is possible that what is meant is what we have mentioned, using it as proof is invalid. And this narrator has narrated what contradicts this report and indicates what I have held.

key_terms.الِاحْتِجَاجَ: using a report as legal proof or evidence
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal understanding
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose presence affects the validity and continuation of tayammum
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), used here by comparison with renewing purification
key_terms.بِتَيَمُّمٍ: by tayammum, the dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable
key_terms.لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ: for every salat (prayer), indicating repetition of tayammum per prayer in one report
key_terms.نَافِلَتُهَا: its supererogatory prayer, meaning the optional prayer connected to the obligatory one
key_terms.يُحْدِثْ: he breaks his state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Can one tayammum be used for more than one salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the fiqh ruling of tayammum and whether one tayammum may be used for multiple prayers. It presents reports that appear different in wording, then explains that the proof from the restrictive report is weakened and may be understood as recommending renewal of tayammum rather than making it obligatory. The passage is significant for showing hadith comparison and legal reconciliation in Shia fiqh.
